decisions.candidate: ELEMENTOS GERAIS > ALTERAÇÕES DE PESO (PERDA OU GANHO) > Fadiga
decisions.reason: Every utterance states tiredness or exhaustion in the source's own words (cansaço, esgotamento/esgotado, desgaste físico e mental) and that rest or sleep did not relieve it. Fadiga has exactly one context in the inventory.

decisions.candidate: ELEMENTOS GERAIS > ALTERAÇÕES DE PESO (PERDA OU GANHO) > Astenia
decisions.reason: Source line: “Falta persistente de força ou energia, não explicada apenas por esforço.” The utterance opens with “Não é só depois de esforço”, a near-literal echo of this entry's distinguishing clause, and reports tiredness that persists. The same sentence also carries Fadiga's rest clause. The reviewer cannot rank one path clearly above the other from the source text alone.
Source line: “Fraqueza orgânica generalizada, cansaço físico extremo sem esforço proporcional.” “Cansaço [...] sem esforço proporcional” is evoked; generalized weakness and “extremo” are not stated.

decisions.candidate: Astenia (four contexts: ELEMENTOS GERAIS, CARDIOVASCULAR, ENDOCRINOLÓGICO, HEMOLINFOPOIÉTICO)
decisions.reason: None of the four passing utterances states weakness, lack of strength or any relation to effort, which are what the Astenia lines add to tiredness/lack of energy; all four state the rest clause that only the Fadiga line contains. The hemolymphopoietic entry additionally ties tiredness to anaemia, which no utterance mentions. Astenia is not clinically ruled out; it has no distinguishing textual support.

Sleep appears only as the rest that failed to help (“dormir um pouco mais”, “uma noite de sono”, “acordo cansado”). No difficulty sleeping, excessive sleepiness or other change of sleep pattern is reported.

Rereading a page is attributed by the speaker to mental exhaustion. No difficulty decoding or spelling words (Dislexia) and no confusion, slowed thought or reduced awareness of surroundings (Obnubilação) is stated.

decisions.candidate: APARELHO PSÍQUICO > Tristeza; APARELHO ENDOCRINOLÓGICO > Apatia; APARELHO NEUROLÓGICO > Paresias; Dispneia entries
decisions.reason: No sadness, discouragement, low self-esteem, apathy, focal muscle weakness or breathing difficulty is stated in any of the five utterances.

findings.issue: “Não é só depois de esforço: acordo cansado e sigo assim mesmo quando tiro um tempo para repousar.” combines the distinguishing clause of Fadiga (“não melhora significativamente com o repouso”) with a near-literal echo of the distinguishing clause of Astenia (“não explicada apenas por esforço”), printed on the next line of the same subgroup. The story accepts only Fadiga. The apostila itself uses “cansaço” in two Astenia descriptions (p.7, p.8), so “cansado” does not settle the choice.

findings.issue: MeSH (D005221) e DeCS (5325) descrevem Fadiga como estado de cansaço/esgotamento que se segue a um período de esforço mental ou físico, com queda da capacidade de trabalho; a apostila (p.1) a descreve como sensação persistente de cansaço, esgotamento físico ou mental e falta de energia que não melhora significativamente com o repouso. A cláusula do repouso é da apostila, não do descritor. A classificação aqui é descritiva e fonte-específica: não certifica causa, duração clínica, doença de base nem alteração de peso.
findings.resolution: Accept source-based descriptive recognition for the passing items. The batch label definitionBasis “source-description-with-verified-terminology” is preserved unchanged, but the opened descriptor verifies the term and its general meaning only, not the apostila's rest clause. MeSH and DeCS list Fatigue and Asthenia as related (“See Also”) descriptors, which is consistent with treating them as close neighbours.

findings.issue: ALTERAÇÕES DE PESO (PERDA OU GANHO) is the printed subgroup under which the apostila lists Fadiga; it is not a clinical statement that the speaker lost or gained weight, and no utterance mentions weight.

source.locator: ELEMENTOS GERAIS > ALTERAÇÕES DE PESO (PERDA OU GANHO) > Fadiga

evidence.quote: Fadiga: sensação persistente de cansaço, esgotamento físico ou mental e falta de energia, que não melhora significativamente com o repouso.

findings.resolution: Keep the literal source mapping and distinguish it from any conclusion about weight change.

findings.issue: The four passing utterances are separated from Astenia only by source wording: they say cansaço/esgotamento/desgaste plus failed rest (Fadiga line) and never fraqueza, falta de força or esforço (Astenia lines). “Falta de energia” is printed in both the Fadiga line and two Astenia lines, so the boundary between the two terms is narrow in the apostila itself. Index 25 (“Passei a tarde quieta”) is the closest of the four to the endocrinological Astenia wording (“cansaço físico extremo sem esforço proporcional”).
findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with accepting only Fadiga for these four: the rest clause is literal in each and no Astenia-specific element is stated. A teaching reviewer may still want to confirm that a student answering Astenia for plain “cansaço que não passa com descanso” should be scored as incorrect.

findings.issue: Persistence, the first word of the source description, is explicit at indices 27 and 29 (and implied by “acordo [...] e sigo assim” at 26) but only implicit at 25 (“continuaram iguais” after one afternoon) and 28 (habitual present, one night of sleep). Index 28 adds a reading/concentration detail that is not in the source description. Index 27 is slightly formal for speech (“desgaste físico e mental persistente”). All five are single sentences, share the same stock story-level rationale, and record generation model “unknown”.
findings.resolution: Within the stated rules (lay speech, 1–2 paragraphs, technical term not given away, no diagnosis or advice). Recorded as editorial observations only; no change required for the prototype.
